description:
Delete all memories with a specific tag and their embeddings.

Use cases:
- Knowledge base lifecycle management (remove an ingested corpus).
- Cleanup of follow-up queues or heartbeat instruction memories that should no longer exist.
- Implement "replace by tag" semantics by deleting old tagged memories before writing a new canonical memory.

This is destructive and irreversible. Prefer precise tags (e.g., heartbeat:global, followup_queue:session:<id>) and avoid broad tag patterns.
embedding_description: Delete all memories with a specific tag (destructive). Use to clean up stale follow-up queues, remove an obsolete heartbeat instruction memory, or clear an ingested knowledge base corpus. Often paired with writing a replacement memory to implement replace-by-tag semantics.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Result of deleting all memories with the specified tag
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Tagged memories were deleted. If this tag is referenced by a schedule (memory_tag), future wake-ups for that tag will retrieve no instructions; consider whether you should also clear any schedules that reference this tag, or replace the memory with a new canonical instruction.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Deleting all memories with a specific tag
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: DatabaseError: failed to delete memory records. VectorStoreError: failed to delete associated embeddings.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For database errors: verify state storage is accessible. For vector store errors: verify vector storage is accessible.
